title: NVFP4 checkpoint enablement
shape: P3-16 F16K L78K and D3-32 r8 (load + smoke; no kernel timing owned)
basis: MEASURED 1-node P3-16 DEP4 slice, L24 NVFP4 view, dummy weights (runs/EN/step_p/nv-smoke2); unit tests in image
gap_analysis: Enablement, not a kernel family. B1/B1b/B5/B6 done in code + CPU tests: the MegaMoE format follows the ModelOpt quantized_layers entry of each block's experts; megamoe_rubin loads ModelOpt NVFP4 experts natively (E2M1 codes, E4M3 block-16 scales, per-expert weight_scale_2, input_scale) as a pure re-layout with alpha = weight_scale_2 and unit norm constants, which equals the stock NVFP4 MoE math for the export's unit input scales (verified on real scalar scales of 4 layers). Kernel-layout dequant == stock ModelOpt dequant bitwise; NVFP4 export of MXFP4 weights == in-backend exact conversion bitwise. ModelOpt MXFP8 checkpoint linears (shared experts, KDA in/o_proj) now take the kimi_k3 MXFP8 fast paths (per-shape kernel dispatch, packing, producer-fused activation quant), previously keyed on online MXFP8 only. Not yet run on GPU: the pool had no running hold (unit tests + 1-node NVFP4 smoke queued). Decode NVFP4 additionally needs B3 (EP32 NVFP4 knobs/FI re-vendor, D-MOE) and B4 (MXFP8 projections in sdec, D-GEMM).
inefficiencies: NVFP4 expert bytes per expert are ~9% above MXFP4 (E4M3 scale per 16 vs E8M0 per 32): routed-expert weight streaming at decode grows accordingly (model item, not a bug)
An NVFP4 checkpoint forces the NVFP4 kernel kind at every bucket: the MX kind's small-batch advantage (as fast or faster up to 256 tokens/rank at EP16) is unavailable
No EP4 genphase NVFP4 knob records: 1-node slices must run >1024 tokens/rank (inference variant)
rubin_features: NVFP4 block-scaled MMA (E2M1 x E4M3 block-16 scales) via the vendored Rubin MegaMoE
MXFP8 block-scaled GEMM for shared experts / KDA projections
